SMTO-GML-0026 — Gmail authorization expired

GUID: 9e60856b-7cc3-49a9-b10e-de4abe568556
Slug: gmail-reauthorization-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO can no longer use the permission Google gave it for this Gmail account. This message alone does not establish why: it may have expired, been removed, or been refused by Google.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, ask SMTO to connect your Gmail account again, open the Google link, choose the same account and select Allow. Signing in again gives SMTO a fresh permission to replace the one that stopped working.
  2. Wait for the page that says the account is connected and that you can close the window. That message confirms SMTO saved the new permission.
  3. Before asking SMTO to repeat an email send or bulk change, open Gmail and check the Sent folder or the affected emails. Earlier steps of the same task may already have finished, and repeating them could send or change things twice.
  4. If reconnecting doesn't help or Google says access is blocked, select Copy error details. Google may be refusing access because of a policy, which the person who manages SMTO must fix.

What success looks like

  • The Google window says your account is connected, and SMTO can read your Gmail again.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste your Google password, sign-in codes or the Google link into a conversation or screenshot.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail could not use the saved account's authorization: no access token is stored, Google rejected the token refresh, or a Gmail API call still returned 401 after one forced refresh.

What this means

  • Account access lacks a token or refresh/authorization is rejected; compatibility refresh also maps some provider denials to reauthorization_required without proving simple expiration. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Account access lacks a token or refresh/authorization is rejected; compatibility refresh also maps some provider denials to reauthorization_required without proving simple expiration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect missing-token, refresh and provider evidence before assuming the session merely expired.

How to fix it

  • Raised when the Gmail Account parameter has no access token (GmailRestClient), token refresh is rejected (authorized_gmail maps a token-endpoint rejection), or a REST call still returns 401 after one forced refresh (_AuthorizedClient, GmailService._call). Not every case is simple expiry: inspect the provider reason in the Server log; for a missing or revoked grant run gmail.connect again with the same account_key, and if Google denies refresh for policy reasons fix the OAuth App or Workspace access policy first.
  • Use the supported account flow for missing/revoked credentials; inspect the provider reason and access policy when a denial is not proven to be expiration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual authorization problem is resolved for the intended account without replaying uncertain writes.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GML-0036 — Google refused SMTO access to this Gmail request
  • SMTO-GML-0009 — The list of emails to change has expired
  • SMTO-GML-0030 — Gmail mutation outcome is unknown
